item.title: Full text: Keynote speech by Chinese President Xi Jinping at the APEC CEO Summit 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
Full text: Keynote speech by Chinese President Xi Jinping at the APEC CEO Summit 2026 SHENZHEN -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday delivered a keynote speech at the APEC CEO Summit 2026 in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. The following is the full text of the speech: Forging Ahead with Resolve Toward a Bright Future for the Asia-Pacific Keynote Speech by H.E. Xi Jinping President of the People's Republic of China At the APEC CEO Summit Shenzhen, November 18, 2026 Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, Dear Friends, Good morning! I wish to extend my welcome to you all, leaders of business communities of the Asia-Pacific. I am so delighted to meet you here in Shenzhen. Shenzhen, on the shores of the South China Sea, embraces the surging winds and waves of the ocean. Over the past 40 years and more, Shenzhen has been a pioneer in China's pursuit of reform and opening up. It has achieved a historic transformation from a small border town into an international metropolis, creating a miracle in the history of global development. There is so much people can draw from Shenzhen's success. Today, we find ourselves in a changing and turbulent world. Global growth lacks momentum, and unilateralism and protectionism are rampant. Still, global trade keeps growing against headwinds, and breakthroughs are being made in emerging technologies at a faster pace, exerting a profound impact on global development. What is going on with the world? What should we do in the Asia-Pacific? To open doors or close doors, work together or against each other, adapt to change or stick to old ways? These are hard questions of our times that we must answer. As an ancient Chinese saying goes, all approaches should adapt to changing times to remain relevant. Born amid the waves of economic globalization, APEC has enabled the Asia-Pacific to steer the course of our times. This year, China is hosting APEC for the third time. We are ready to work with all other parties to forge ahead with resolve, jointly build an Asia-Pacific community, and bring prosperity for all in our region. -- To bring prosperity for all in the Asia-Pacific, we should uphold peace and stability. There can be no prosperity without security, and no security without stability. Thanks to the stable environment in our region over the past decades, the Asia-Pacific has maintained steady economic progress and become an important engine driving global growth. The more complex the external conditions become, the more important it is for us to uphold the postwar international order, and promote an equality-based and orderly multipolar world and economic globalization that is inclusive and brings benefit to all. It is even more important for us to resolve differences through dialogue and consultation, and overcome challenges through solidarity and cooperation. This is the way to cement the foundation for sustaining peace and stability in the Asia-Pacific. -- To bring prosperity for all in the Asia-Pacific, we should build bridges of opening up and cooperation. History tells us that opening doors brings progress while closing doors leaves one behind. We should firmly safeguard the WTO-centered, rules-based multilateral trading system, support free and open trade and investment, and keep global industrial and supply chains stable and unimpeded. We should work steadily toward a Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific, build a multidimensional connectivity network, enhance cooperation in areas such as digital transformation of trade, cross-border e-commerce, and smart customs, and deepen international cooperation on industrial and supply chains. All this will pave the way for greater economic integration in the Asia-Pacific. -- To bring prosperity for all in the Asia-Pacific, we should boost innovation to drive growth. Innovation is crucial for progress. APEC members have driven global scientific and technological innovation: Unicorn companies and large AI models have emerged in large numbers, and many innovations have empowered hundreds of trades and industries and reached millions of households. We should forge science, technology and innovation partnerships, deepen cooperation in the digital economy and AI, and promote green and low-carbon transition. By doing so, we can turn strengths in innovation into drivers of growth, and provide strong impetus for economic growth in the Asia-Pacific. -- To bring prosperity for all in the Asia-Pacific, we should expand our ways for mutual benefits and win-win outcomes. As the economies in our region differ in history, culture and stage of development, taking a uniform approach will not advance cooperation. We should remove trade and investment barriers to build an open Asia-Pacific economy. At the same time, we should promote development that is balanced and delivers benefits to all to ensure both efficiency and fairness. We should follow a people-centered development philosophy, strengthen economic and technical cooperation geared for developing economies, and deepen cooperation in transportation, public health, energy, food security, anti-corruption and other fields, so that development fruits are shared by all economies and all groups and communities. The Asia-Pacific region is home to the world's most important bay areas notable for their open and interconnected economies with positive spillover effects. Shenzhen, where we are now meeting, is part of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. China supports the establishment of a World Association for Bay Areas Economic Cooperation to deepen exchanges and interactions among bay areas from across the world. This will help us explore new ways for stronger economic cooperation in the Asia-Pacific. Distinguished Guests, Dear Friends, This year marks the start of China's 15th Five-Year Plan for economic and social development. China's economy maintains a strong momentum of high-quality, innovation-driven growth, demonstrating great resilience and vitality. In the first three quarters, the Chinese economy grew by 4.6 percent. New quality productive forces are developing more quickly, a new pattern of development is being fostered at a faster pace, and green and low-carbon transition is steadily picking up speed. The 15th Five-Year Plan has gotten off to a good start. A blueprint for China's development, the 15th Five-Year Plan also provides a list of opportunities for promoting economic growth in the Asia-Pacific and the wider world. Indeed, it is an invitation for cooperation China has sent to business communities from around the world. -- China will provide global business communities with a super-sized open market. China is the world's second largest consumer market. It has the largest middle income group in the world and enormous potential for investment and consumption. From new energy vehicles to smart homes, from the silver economy to ice and snow tourism, every new growth area is creating new opportunities for businesses across the world. As China accelerates the development of a big, open market and increases import of quality products and services, more diverse demands will be unleashed. Recently, the ninth China International Import Expo was held in Shanghai. Many of you present today attended the Expo and found new cooperation opportunities. China will also continue to host "Export to China" series and other events to open efficient channels to help quality products from across the world enter the Chinese market. -- China will provide global business communities with a promising land for development. Innovation-driven growth and green transition are the keywords in observing China's economy. From factory and farm robots, to autonomous driving and drone delivery, China is a super-sized innovation testing ground where frontier technologies are tested, improved and upgraded in real-world scenarios, and are then turned into high-quality growth drivers. China will step up efforts to build modernized industrial system, and deepen integration between technological and industrial innovation. It will support the transformation and upgrading of traditional industries, the expansion of emerging industries, and the forward-looking planning of industries of the future. This will generate strong impetus for technological innovation and growth of businesses around the world. -- China will provide global business communities with an environment that enables mutually reinforcing cooperation. In 2001, China hosted the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting for the first time and joined the World Trade Organization in the same year. Over the past 25 years, China has fully honored its WTO accession commitments. While pursuing its own development, China has shared opportunities with other countries and worked for common development. China has stood up to unilateralism and protectionism, and remained committed to true multilateralism, to upholding the multilateral trading system and WTO rules, and to advancing WTO reform; it has steadily brought stability and predictability to world economic growth and international trade and economic cooperation. No matter how the international landscape may evolve, China will not waver in its pursuit of win-win cooperation with all other countries. China stays firmly committed to high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, and welcomes the active participation of businesses from across the Asia-Pacific so that we can create growth opportunities and share the fruits of development together. China will not only cut tariffs and expand market access but also go a step further -- we will carry out reform in challenging areas, such as rules, regulation and standards, in order to fully ensure market access and an accommodating operating environment in the manufacturing sector, to steadily expand opening up in the service sector, and to foster a more stable and more predictable first-class environment for companies from around the world to invest and do business in China. Distinguished Guests, Dear Friends, The Asia-Pacific is our home; it is here we jointly pursue development and cooperation. Asia-Pacific business communities are pioneers of the global economy. I hope you will carry forward the entrepreneurial spirit, boldly pursue innovation and excellence, explore and expand opportunities for business cooperation, and make greater contributions to economic integration in the Asia-Pacific. You are more than welcome to continue to get actively involved in China's reform and opening up and modernization drive, and share in the opportunities created by Chinese modernization. Let us join hands to meet challenges facing development through opening up, generate momentum for growth through innovation, and pursue prosperity for all through cooperation. Let us work together to build an Asia-Pacific community and deliver a bright future for our region. Thank you.

item.title: Xi calls for joint efforts to develop China-Chile ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
Xi calls for joint efforts to develop China-Chile ties Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 17, 2026. [Xinhua/Shen Hong] SHENZHEN -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said Tuesday that he is ready to work with Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast to strengthen strategic guidance, keep to the right direction, and jointly draw a blueprint for the growth of bilateral relations, so as to support the development and prosperity of the two countries. Xi made the remarks during his meeting with Kast in Shenzhen. The Chilean president is in the southern Chinese city to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov. 18-19. Noting that Chile was the first South American country to establish diplomatic relations with the People's Republic of China, Xi said the bilateral ties had withstood the test of a changing international landscape and maintained sound and steady development for a long time. The most valuable experience is that the two sides respect each other, treat each other as equals, and pursue win-win outcomes, he said. As this year marks the 10th anniversary of the establishment of the China-Chile comprehensive strategic partnership and the 20th anniversary of the entry into force of the China-Chile Free Trade Agreement, the bilateral relations have reached an important juncture for building on past achievements and forging ahead into the future, Xi said. Xi noted that China and Chile should continue to support each other on issues concerning their respective core interests and major concerns, strengthen exchanges across multiple sectors and at various levels, and share experience in state governance. Given the complementarity of their economies and the solid foundation of their cooperation, the two countries should better align their development strategies through high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, promote traditional cooperation in trade, energy, minerals, infrastructure and astronomic research, and expand into emerging fields such as artificial intelligence (AI), polar scientific expeditions, and deep-sea exploration, Xi said. He stressed that China stands ready to enhance communication and coordination with Chile within multilateral frameworks such as APEC, jointly uphold true multilateralism, and act as defenders of the common interests of developing countries. China is willing to work with Latin American and Caribbean (LAC) countries to inject greater certainty into peace and development in the region, and push forward China-LAC cooperation, Xi said. Kast stated that since the establishment of diplomatic relations between Chile and China, their bilateral ties have developed steadily, regardless of changes in the international landscape. For many years, China has remained Chile's largest trading partner and the leading destination for its agricultural and mineral exports. Cooperation with China has provided important opportunities for Chile's economic and social development, and strengthening ties with China represents a consensus across all sectors of Chilean society, the president added. Chile will unswervingly adhere to the one-China policy, deepen its good relations with China, expand the scale of trade and investment cooperation, broaden collaboration in agriculture, mining, new energy vehicles, infrastructure development and AI, and promote exchanges in education and culture, Kast noted. Chile stands ready to strengthen coordination with China within multilateral frameworks such as APEC, uphold multilateralism, remain committed to free trade, and promote peace and development worldwide, he said. Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 17, 2026. [Xinhua/Yan Yan]

item.title: Xi calls for advancing steady, sound development of China-ROK relations
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
Xi calls for advancing steady, sound development of China-ROK relations Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with President of the Republic of Korea (ROK) Lee Jae Myung, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 18, 2026. [Xinhua/Wang Ye] SHENZHEN -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday called for advancing the steady and sound development of relations between China and the Republic of Korea (ROK) as next year marks the 35th anniversary of diplomatic ties between the two "friendly neighbors and strategic cooperative partners." Xi made the remarks during his meeting with ROK President Lee Jae Myung, who is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting on Nov. 18-19. The two countries should uphold strategic independence, maintain the political foundation for bilateral relations, and further consolidate and develop the relationship, Xi stressed. China and the ROK have substantially concluded the second phase of negotiations on the China-ROK Free Trade Agreement. The two countries should make full use of this institutional arrangement to strengthen macroeconomic policy coordination and foster a collaborative ecosystem for emerging technology industries such as artificial intelligence, Xi said. China also stands ready to work with the ROK to facilitate people-to-people exchanges and carry out sound and beneficial cultural exchanges in a step-by-step manner, Xi said. The two sides should further strengthen multilateral coordination, jointly uphold true multilateralism, advance the building of an Asia-Pacific community and the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific, make greater contributions to regional peace and development, and maintain the stability and smooth functioning of global industrial and supply chains, Xi said. For his part, Lee said that the two countries have seen sustained momentum in the comprehensive restoration of ROK-China relations, with bilateral economic and trade cooperation growing rapidly, people-to-people exchanges becoming increasingly frequent, and mutual perceptions steadily improving. The ROK's commitment to the one-China policy has not changed and will not change, Lee stressed. The ROK hopes to maintain close high-level exchanges with China, strengthen cooperation in trade, investment, and industrial and supply chains, foster closer people-to-people bonds, and pursue a more mature ROK-China strategic partnership, he said. Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with President of the Republic of Korea (ROK) Lee Jae Myung, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 18, 2026. [Xinhua/Tian Yu]

item.title: Xi says China-Russia relations bring stability, certainty to turbulent world
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
Xi says China-Russia relations bring stability, certainty to turbulent world Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Russian President Vladimir Putin, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 18, 2026. [Xinhua/Wang Ye] SHENZHEN -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said Wednesday that China-Russia relations have brought greater stability and certainty to a world of turbulence and transformation. Xi made the remarks while meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin, who is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting on Nov. 18-19. Xi noted that this year marks the 30th anniversary of the establishment of the China-Russia strategic partnership of coordination and the 25th anniversary of the signing of the China-Russia Treaty of Good-Neighborliness and Friendly Cooperation. He said that China-Russia ties set an example for a new model of major-country relations featuring equality, mutual respect, good faith, and win-win cooperation. Xi called on both countries to deepen all-round cooperation and firmly uphold the due responsibilities and obligations of major countries to guide and promote a multipolar world and democratization of international relations. Both sides should leverage the mechanisms for exchanges between their governments, legislatures, militaries and political parties to ensure that the consensus reached by the two heads of state is effectively implemented, Xi said. Xi called on the two countries to provide a more stable and predictable investment and business environment and protect the legitimate rights and interests of enterprises from both countries. The development of China and Russia is closely intertwined with that of the Asia-Pacific region, and APEC is an important platform for enhancing cooperation, Xi noted. China stands ready to work with the Asia-Pacific family, including Russia, to chart a course for the region's prosperity and development and build an Asia-Pacific community together, Xi said. Putin said he and Xi have held four productive meetings so far this year, helping sustain the sound development momentum in Russia-China relations. High-level exchanges have been close, bilateral trade has reached a new high, and practical cooperation has made substantial progress across various fields, he said. Russia is willing to strengthen back-to-back strategic coordination with China, expand cooperation in trade, energy, education and other fields, and broaden cultural and people-to-people exchanges to better benefit the two peoples, Putin said. Russia also stands ready to work with China to promote development and cooperation in the Asia-Pacific, advance the process toward a multipolar world and build a more just and equitable global governance system, he added. Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Russian President Vladimir Putin, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 18, 2026. [Xinhua/Tian Yu]

item.title: Xi calls for jointly building Asia-Pacific community to prosper together
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18
Xi calls for jointly building Asia-Pacific community to prosper together Chinese President Xi Jinping delivers a keynote speech at the opening ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026 at the Qianhai International Convention Center in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 18, 2026. [Xinhua/Li Tao] SHENZHEN -- Chinese President Xi Jinping pledged on Wednesday that China is willing to work with all parties to forge ahead with resolve, jointly build an Asia-Pacific community and bring prosperity for all. Addressing the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026 in the southern metropolis of Shenzhen, Xi called on business communities in the region to uphold the entrepreneurial spirit and make greater contributions to economic integration in the Asia-Pacific. Under the theme "To Prosper and Win the Future Together," the two-day summit has attracted more than 2,000 representatives from 21 APEC economies and 13 non-APEC economies, including Britain, France, Germany and Switzerland. "The Asia-Pacific is our home; it is here we jointly pursue development and cooperation," Xi said. Born amid the waves of economic globalization, APEC has been one of the world's most dynamic engines of growth. Today, the APEC economies are home to about 40 percent of the world's population, and account for more than 60 percent of global GDP and nearly half of global trade. As the world becomes more turbulent and the global economy lacks growth momentum, the Chinese president said the region must answer the "hard questions of our times": to open doors or close doors, work together or against each other, adapt to change or stick to old ways? In his response, Xi put forward proposals on how the region can prosper together, calling on APEC economies to uphold peace and stability, build bridges of opening up and cooperation, boost innovation to drive growth and expand ways for mutual benefits and win-win outcomes. All parties in the region must "uphold the postwar international order," he said, calling on them to resolve differences through dialogue and consultation and address challenges through solidarity and coordination. Xi said the Asia-Pacific should support free and open trade and investment while keeping the global industrial and supply chains stable and unimpeded. "History tells us that opening doors brings progress while closing doors leaves one behind," he said, calling for efforts to steadily advance the process of the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific. He stressed the need to forge partnerships in science, technology and innovation, deepen cooperation in the digital economy and artificial intelligence, and promote green and low-carbon development. "By doing so, we can turn strengths in innovation into drivers of growth, and provide strong impetus for economic growth in the Asia-Pacific," the president said. The region should also remove trade and investment barriers to build an open Asia-Pacific economy, and promote development that is balanced and delivers benefits to all to ensure both efficiency and fairness, Xi said. According to Xi, there is much to draw from the success of Shenzhen, host of this year's APEC CEO Summit and the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting. Over the past 40 years and more, Shenzhen has been a pioneer in China's pursuit of reform and opening up. It has achieved a historic transformation from a small border town into an international metropolis, creating a miracle in the history of global development, Xi said. Noting that the Asia-Pacific region is home to the world's most important bay areas notable for their open and interconnected economies with positive spillover effects, Xi said China supports the establishment of a World Association for Bay Areas Economic Cooperation to deepen exchanges and interactions among bay areas from across the world. "This will help us explore new ways for stronger economic cooperation in the Asia-Pacific," he said. Looking ahead, as China's ties with the Asia-Pacific grow increasingly close, Xi said China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) provides a list of opportunities for promoting economic growth in the Asia-Pacific and the wider world. The development blueprint is "an invitation for cooperation China has sent to business communities from around the world," he said. Xi said China will provide the global business community with a super-sized open market, a promising land for development, as well as an environment that enables mutually reinforcing cooperation. He highlighted China's accelerating efforts to develop a big, open market and build a modern industrial system, pledging a more stable and predictable first-class environment for companies from around the world to invest and do business in China. Calling the Asia-Pacific business communities "pioneers of the global economy," he said they are "more than welcome to continue to get actively involved in China's reform and opening up and modernization drive, and share in the opportunities created by Chinese modernization." Leaders of APEC economies, including Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, attended the summit. Having previously hosted the APEC Economic Leaders' Meetings in 2001 and 2014, China is taking on the role of APEC host for the third time this year. It has hosted more than 300 APEC meetings and events this year and reached nearly 50 practical outcomes with other APEC economies in the economic and trade field. item.title: Accelerating the Building of a Healthy China
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
Accelerating the Building of a Healthy China Accelerating the Building of a Healthy China XI JINPING The Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) has made the strategic decision to build a Healthy China by 2035, and the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030) is a critical window for achieving this goal. We must take a coordinated approach to planning and press ahead with urgency to secure decisive progress toward this goal. First, medical and health services should be developed in light of China’s realities China is a developing socialist country with a vast population where considerable disparities still persist between urban and rural areas and among regions. These realities dictate that we follow a path of health development with distinctive Chinese characteristics, ensuring that our Party exercises leadership over health work, putting the people and their lives above all else, implementing a health-first strategy, and seeing that basic medical and health services are oriented toward the public interest. At the National Health Conference in 2016, the CPC Central Committee put forward the guidelines for health development in the new era: giving priority to community-level services, using reform and innovation to drive progress, putting prevention first, placing equal emphasis on Western medicine and traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), incorporating health considerations into all policies, and ensuring the people contribute to and benefit from the development of health care. The profound achievements in China’s health sector since the advent of the new era in 2012 are ample proof that these guidelines are well-suited to China’s national context and are entirely correct. Both now and in the period ahead, specific health work policies and measures will need to be adjusted and refined in response to changing circumstances. What we must not waver in, however, is our commitment to following the path of health development with Chinese characteristics or implementing the guidelines for health work in the new era. On these fundamental issues, we must remain clear-headed and maintain strategic resolve. General Secretary Xi Jinping visits national political advisors from the Chinese Peasants and Workers Democratic Party, the Jiusan Society, the sector of medicine and health, and the sector of social welfare and social security, who are attending the fourth session of the 14th National Committee of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference, Beijing, afternoon of March 6, 2026. Xi attended their joint group meeting to hear their comments and suggestions. PHOTO BY XINHUA REPORTER XIE HUANCHI Second, priority should be placed on key areas in advancing the Healthy China Initiative Building a Healthy China is a systematic endeavor. As people’s medical and healthcare needs grow and diversify, we should focus on what will benefit the population broadly and have a far-reaching impact across the entire health sector. Both our efforts and resources should be concentrated on such tasks to deliver further progress. For instance, improving the public health system requires deepening public participation, strengthening coordination and integration of medical care and disease prevention initiatives, and reinforcing epidemic prevention and control, monitoring and early warning, medical treatment, emergency response, supply provision, and oversight and management. We should also attach great importance to mental health and psychiatric care, strengthening preventive guidance, early detection, and comprehensive intervention. General Secretary Xi Jinping talks with medical staff at the community health station of the CPC-led community service center, Changcheng Huayuan Community, Jinfeng District, Yinchuan City, afternoon of June 19, 2024. Xi visited Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region on an inspection tour on June 19 and 20. PHOTO BY XINHUA REPORTER XIE HUANCHI Another example is meeting the people’s growing expectations for a high-quality and efficient medical service system. We should continue to improve the layout of the system, carry out capacity-building projects for community-level health care, promote tiered diagnosis and treatment, and strengthen operational support for medical and health institutions at the county, district, and community levels. We should also promote integrated application of TCM and Western medicine, shore up weak links in services for key populations and under-resourced specialties, strengthen comprehensive prevention and control of chronic diseases, and expand the provision of services such as rehabilitative care and palliative care. A further example is the promotion of healthy and wholesome lifestyles. In this regard, we need to further raise public health literacy, advance public fitness initiatives and patriotic health campaigns, and guide people to maintain balanced diets and better manage their weight. Each of these tasks must be backed by concrete steps and levers. If these key tasks are carried out effectively, we will make solid progress in building a Healthy China. Third, strong institutional support should be provided to build a Healthy China This requires us to improve the working mechanism under which Party committees exercise overall leadership and Party and government departments work in tandem, refine the framework of policies and institutions for promoting people’s health, and make sure the principle of health promotion is embedded in the entire public policy process from formulation to implementation. We should deepen the reform of public hospitals and medical insurance payment models, improve the drug pricing mechanism, refine centralized procurement policies for medicines and medical consumables, ensure efficient use of medical insurance funds, and enhance the mechanisms for promoting coordinated development and governance of medical services, medical insurance, and pharmaceuticals. We should encourage the application of scientific and technological advances in the health sector and use digital and intelligent technologies to improve public health. Moreover, we should strengthen Party organizations in the health sector, keep healthcare workers motivated and spur their creativity, step up the training and development of healthcare professionals, promote sound ethics and professional conduct, and cultivate a culture of integrity across the medical profession. Building a Healthy China calls for broad participation from across society. The Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference should play its role as a specialized consultative body, conducting in-depth surveys and studies on relevant issues, both theoretical and practical, and putting forward targeted and effective suggestions. Members of the Chinese Peasants and Workers Democratic Party and the Jiusan Society, along with people working in the medicine and health sector and the social welfare and social security sector, should fully leverage their professional expertise to contribute their wisdom and energy to building a Healthy China. This is the main part of remarks made by General Secretary Xi Jinping on March 6, 2026, at a joint group meeting of members of the Chinese Peasants and Workers Democratic Party, the Jiusan Society, the medicine and health sector, and the social welfare and social security sector at the fourth session of the 14th National Committee of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference. (Originally appeared in Qiushi Journal, Chinese edition, No. 15, 2026)
